Controls

The controls are very basic, WASD to move, Left mouse button to shoot your gun, Right mouse button to activate your anti-gravity tractor beam device thingy majig. If I have any complaints about the controls, it's that the game doesn't seem to be designed for a mouse with a high(ish) DPI. I've got a 3,200 dpi laser mouse, It's not the highest DPI out there, but the game seems over sensitive and twitchy. You can control mouse sensitivity in game, but it didn't help me much. Overall, I like the controls though, 4 keys and 2 buttons, simplicity at it's best.

Artistic Quality/Graphics

Ok, I'll talk about the aesthetics here (but not the physics engine yet). This game is cartoony. The main character, BEEP, reminds me of WALL-E, and the game makes me feel childish... which is a good thing. The art style of this game is just charming. Down to the little details like how BEEP's eyes change to "Angry" when firing his weapon or "Worried" when in mid air... it's just adorable.

Storyline

Ok, the storyline. Not great, it is there simply to lead you on from one puzzle to the next. The game takes place through different "Worlds".

There are 3 worlds which are made up of 8 levels, split into 2 themes, for example, the last world has 4 ice levels and 4 lava levels.

To travel from one level to the next, or to re-play previous levels, you must control your ship (With your mouse button) between planets, it's an interesting level menu but the gimmick wears off, and you sometimes find yourself wishing you had a simple list of levels.

The humour is decent, giving hints with jokes on hint pads throughout the levels, but that isn't where the game shines.

Audio

The sound effects are great, BEEP usually speaks in... beeps. But has the ability to speak in English, saying phrases like "Tasty!" and "That's just perfect.", BEEP always sounds adorable, though, and that's a very charming thing. When he defeats an enemy, he gives out a kind of robot giggle that never fails to warm my heart.

The music is chilled out and relaxing, it changes when you are in battle (which does raise the tension) or for certain other things, but often you will find the music stops completely... which is a bit of a shame. The music, although very good, does it's job perfectly as supporting the game, not outshining it. So the music often fades into the back of your mind.

Game play/Physics Engine

I'm going to have to put the game play and physics engine in the same section, because the game play does depend so much on the physics engine.

Now, for the earlier levels, the physics is fine, it's very sensitive (With the problems with the mouse not helping) but you do not need a great deal of accuracy and precision.

However, the physics engine really does start to irritate when you are on the later levels which make you stack 4-6 slippery objects to get to a goal. It's not fun any more when you're trying to stack multiple objects for hours, literally, and they just fall over as soon as you get near them.

This is not, however, a massive problem. As you do not have to collect objectives to pass the level, so you can always leave "anti matter" behind (Anti-matter being the 'coins' of this particular platform puzzler).

It is slightly frustrating to know how to get an antimatter and be unable to do so because of the limitations of the physics engine.

The length of the game isn't massive. There are 24 levels, I am at level 21 and I have spent 4.5 hours on the game, keep in mind the first 4 levels are incredibly easy and fast. I would say you can complete the game in about 5.5 hours and maybe 100% complete it (with all anti-matter) in about 7 hours... (Although I won't be playing to do that as the anti-matter I have left is so irritating to get to.)

5.5-7 hours isn't really long, but it's longer than some games which cost 5-6 times the price.

Price

At £0.79 ($1) this game is cheap, and even for the first 16 levels, before the problems start kicking in with the over-sensitivity with the mouse/physics, I would say you are getting your money's worth. Keep in mind this game is often heavily discounted as well.

Conclusion

If you are a fan of Platform/Puzzlers, I recommend this game, the puzzles are not too difficult, but will challenge you all the same, and the platforming is good old fashioned style, but with a little twist.

Performance

I have a pretty middle of the range computer, 3.2ghz quad core processor gtx 460 and 4gb ram and this game runs fine, the only performance issues I get was when great deals of shrapnel are on the screen from multiple explosions, which is very rare.

Rating

I would have to give this game a rating of 7/10.

Definitely worth the £0.79 it is asking for, and always good to support an indie developer.
